subject: SLO acceptance synthesis and decision checklist (p95/p99) — next steps
messages:
From: Aaron Cole <aaron@orchidhealth.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Tess (SRE) <tess@sre-orchid.com>, Procurement <procurement@orchidhealth.com>
Date: Wed, 2 Jun 2027 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call summary: latency targets and next steps

Rishi / Marissa — thanks for the call this morning. Quick recap from our side and asks so we can make momentum toward a decision: 

Summary of what matters to us
- p95 end-to-end (API front-door to response complete) target: 120ms for short requests (prompt <= 256 tokens)
- p99 target: <= 350ms, but must understand per-region variance
- Sustained throughput target: 200 rps (avg) with bursts to 600 rps for 2–5 minute windows
- Streaming: we will use server-sent chunked responses for long responses; we care about first-byte latency (initial chunk within 60ms) and steady chunk cadence (every ~50–100ms for streaming tokens)

Immediate asks (what we need from Redwood)
1) A one-page acceptance checklist that maps your runtimes/variants to our p95/p99 numbers and the measurement method (what telemetry, sampling, and synthetic harness you recommend).
2) A short-run demo plan (30–60 minutes) that exercises: short prompt path, streaming steady-state, and burst envelope. Include what data you need from us (sample prompts, token distribution).
3) Any known tradeoffs (quantization, batching, regional fallbacks) that would change p95/p99 numbers so we can evaluate risk.

Attachments: I attached a quick traffic sketch and token-distribution XLSX (see attached).

Thanks — happy to align on timing. We are aiming for a vendor decision by end of June.

— Aaron
[Attachment: orchid_traffic_sketch.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Aaron Cole <aaron@orchidhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>, Procurement <procurement@orchidhealth.com>
Date: Wed, 2 Jun 2027 17:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call summary: latency targets and next steps

Aaron — thanks for the clear recap and timeline. We can do this. High-level responses inline, plus proposed next steps.

Quick responses to asks
1) Acceptance checklist: we will produce a one-page "SLO acceptance checklist" that explicitly maps measurement points (client-side vs edge vs model service), measurement windows, and tolerance bands for p95/p99. We'll include the telemetry keys you should expect in span traces and how to correlate tokens to end-to-end duration.

2) Demo plan: propose a two-phase demo this week:
  - Phase A (30m): short-prompt steady-state + p95 sampling (load generator at 200 rps sustained for 10 minutes).
  - Phase B (45m): burst envelope + streaming sanity (simulated bursts to 600 rps and 10 concurrent streaming clients to validate first-byte and cadence).

For the demo we need: a) a representative set of ~40 short prompts and 8 long streaming prompts, b) target region (we'll run in us-west-2), c) an IP allowlist for our demo harness if you want it to hit your staging endpoints.

3) Tradeoffs:
  - Batching: improves throughput and cost but increases median for short prompts if batching window > 5ms — we will show tradeoff curves during demo.
  - KV-cache/prefix cache helps for repeated prefixes (chat) and can sharply reduce p95; if you rely on chat-heavy patterns we should enable it.
  - Quantization: 4-bit/8-bit variants reduce latency marginally but may impact generation distribution; we'll show a controlled compare.

Proposed next steps
- Send the sample prompts + token distribution (you already sent a sketch — can you confirm the XLSX has the final distribution?).
- We’ll send the checklist and a demo slot proposal (two options) by EOD tomorrow.
- If procurement needs an initial SOW scope for the demo, Marissa can draft one — Marissa, can you take that?

Thanks — Rishi

--
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
rishi@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0142

From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Aaron Cole <aaron@orchidhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Tess (SRE) <tess@sre-orchid.com>
Date: Thu, 3 Jun 2027 01:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call summary: latency targets and next steps

Aaron / team — quick technical notes on how we'll validate p95/p99 end-to-end and a couple clarifying Qs: 

Validation approach (short):
- We will run a client-side load generator (locust-based) from a test VM in us-west-2 to emulate your routing and network conditions.
- Measurements: client-observed request-to-last-byte (this is our baseline for "end-to-end"). We'll also capture edge ingress timestamps and model start/end for correlation.
- Sampling: for p99 we recommend hybrid approach: continuous low-rate sampling + synthetic probes during demo windows to stabilize tail estimates.

Clarifying questions:
- Can you confirm whether your real traffic goes through an internal CDN or is direct to the API gateway? That changes the network hop count and expected p99 headroom.
- For streaming cadence: are you measuring first token latency or first chunk (i.e., our system may emit a small header chunk quickly, then tokens)? We can align to whichever you use in your client metrics.

Notes on load shaping for the demo:
- We'll hold 200 rps steady for 10 minutes for the p95 sampling.
- We'll replay a 5-minute burst pattern (600 rps peak) three times to get variance.

I'll attach a short probe plan and the expected harness commands.

— Jordan
[Attachment: p95_p99_probe_plan.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

From: Aaron Cole <aaron@orchidhealth.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Post-call summary: latency targets and next steps

Appreciate the fast turnaround and the clarity. Quick confirmations: 
- Traffic goes direct to our API Gateway (no CDN).
- Streaming measurement: first meaningful token is what we use (not tiny header chunks).

Next items from us:
- We will send the final sample prompts (40 short / 8 long) and the finalized token distribution XLSX by EOD today.
- Procurement: please send any SOW draft you have for the demo + a short T&Cs summary we can share internally.

Preferred demo windows: Thu 6/3 3pm PT or Fri 6/4 9am PT — either works. We are ok with us-west-2 for tests.

If you can send the one-page acceptance checklist and probe plan before the demo, we will prioritize sign-off. Goal remains vendor decision by end of June.

— Aaron
